**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name:  Eleanor Vance
Age/Gender: 50/Female
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023
Admitting Diagnosis:  Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
Discharge Diagnosis:  STEMI, anterior wall;  Left Ventricular Dysfunction;  Hyperlipidemia;  Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus


**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 00:15]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit: Chest pain, shortness of breath
Interventions: ECG, cardiac biomarkers (troponin I, CK-MB), chest X-ray, 12-lead ECG, oxygen saturation monitoring.  IV access established.
Findings/Results: ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V2-V4, consistent with anterior wall STEMI. Troponin I elevated significantly (15 ng/mL). Chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary pathology.  Oxygen saturation 92% on room air.
Treatment Plan: Immediate transfer to cardiac catheterization lab for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).  Aspirin 325mg chewed, Clopidogrel 300mg loading dose, Morphine sulfate for pain control as needed, Oxygen therapy titrated to maintain SpO2 >95%.


**[October 26, 2023, 02:00]**

Provider Role: Interventional Cardiologist
Reason for Visit:  PCI
Interventions: Coronary angiography revealed a 90% occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery.  Successful PCI with stent placement in the LAD.
Findings/Results:  Post-PCI angiogram showed excellent result with TIMI flow grade 3 in the LAD.
Treatment Plan: Continue aspirin, clopidogrel, and statin therapy.  Cardiac monitoring.


**[October 27, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Cardiology Fellow
Reason for Visit:  Post-PCI assessment
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of cardiac enzymes, echocardiogram.
Findings/Results:  Patient stable, minimal chest pain.  Echocardiogram showed reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%, consistent with left ventricular dysfunction.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate Metoprolol succinate for beta-blockade, Atorvastatin for lipid lowering, and Metformin for glucose control.


**[October 30, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Cardiologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up,  worsening shortness of breath
Interventions:  Physical examination, repeat ECG, chest X-ray, blood work (complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function).
Findings/Results:  Patient reports increased shortness of breath on exertion.  ECG showed no new ST-segment changes.  Chest X-ray showed mild pulmonary edema.  Blood work revealed elevated white blood cell count (12,000/µL), suggesting possible infection.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate intravenous diuretics (Furosemide) for pulmonary edema management.  Broad-spectrum antibiotics (Ceftriaxone) started empirically pending culture results.


**[November 2, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Infectious Disease Consultant
Reason for Visit:  Consultation for suspected infection.
Interventions: Review of cultures.
Findings/Results: Blood cultures grew *Staphylococcus aureus*, sensitive to Ceftriaxone.
Treatment Plan:  Continue Ceftriaxone for 10 days.


**[November 10, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Cardiologist
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of echocardiogram, review of medications.
Findings/Results:  Patient clinically improved, shortness of breath resolved.  LVEF remains at 35%.
Treatment Plan:  Continue all medications.  Cardiac rehabilitation program recommended.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* STEMI with successful PCI on October 26, 2023.
* Development of pulmonary edema and suspected infection on October 30, 2023.
* Diagnosis of *Staphylococcus aureus* bacteremia on November 2, 2023.  Successful treatment with antibiotics.
* Persistent left ventricular dysfunction.

**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

Throughout her hospitalization, Ms. Vance received continuous cardiac monitoring, intravenous fluids, pain management, and supportive care.  She received multiple medications including aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, metformin, furosemide, and ceftriaxone.


**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications: Aspirin 81mg daily, Clopidogrel 75mg daily, Metoprolol Succinate 50mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg daily, Metformin 1000mg BID.

Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with cardiologist in one week.  Cardiac rehabilitation program referral.  Close monitoring of blood glucose and lipids.

Prognosis:  Stable, with ongoing risk for future cardiac events.  Prognosis is guarded, depending on adherence to medication regimen and participation in cardiac rehabilitation.  Long-term management of hyperlipidemia and diabetes mellitus will be crucial.

Provider Role: Cardiology Nurse Practitioner
Reason for Visit:  Phone call – concern regarding increased fatigue and slight swelling in ankles.
Interventions:  Telephone assessment, review of symptoms, medication reconciliation.

Provider Observations:  Mild ankle swelling could be related to medication side effects or early signs of heart failure.  Further investigation warranted.
Treatment Plan:  Advised patient to increase fluid intake and elevate her legs when resting.  Scheduled an in-person follow-up appointment for tomorrow to assess for signs of heart failure (weight gain, increased shortness of breath) and to re-check blood pressure.  Patient instructed to monitor daily weight.


**[December 2, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Cardiologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up appointment – assessment of ankle swelling and fatigue.
Interventions:  Physical examination,  weight measurement, blood pressure monitoring,  blood work (complete blood count,  electrolytes,  renal function,  BNP).
Findings/Results:  Patient reports continued fatigue, but ankle swelling has improved slightly.  Weight has increased by 2 pounds since last visit.  Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg.  BNP level elevated at 250 pg/mL (indicative of mild heart failure).  Blood work otherwise unremarkable.
Provider Observations:  Elevated BNP level and weight gain suggest worsening heart failure.  Requires closer monitoring and possible medication adjustments.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate low-dose Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) for heart failure management.  Increase Metoprolol Succinate to 75mg daily.  Close follow up in one week to monitor for improvement in symptoms and repeat BNP.  Patient educated on signs and symptoms of worsening heart failure and instructed to contact office immediately if symptoms worsen.

* STEMI with successful PCI on October 26, 2023.
* Development of pulmonary edema and suspected infection on October 30, 2023.
* Diagnosis of *Staphylococcus aureus* bacteremia on November 2, 2023.  Successful treatment with antibiotics.
* Persistent left ventricular dysfunction.
* Development of mild heart failure symptoms in December 2023, managed with Lisinopril and increased Metoprolol.


**4. Ongoing Management and Care** *(Existing Note Entry, needs update)*

Throughout her hospitalization, Ms. Vance received continuous cardiac monitoring, intravenous fluids, pain management, and supportive care.  She received multiple medications including aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, metformin, furosemide, and ceftriaxone.  Post-discharge, she is managed with aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, metformin, and now Lisinopril.

**5. Discharge Summary** *(Existing Note Entry, needs update)*

Discharge Medications: Aspirin 81mg daily, Clopidogrel 75mg daily, Metoprolol Succinate 75mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg daily, Metformin 1000mg BID, Lisinopril 2.5mg daily.

Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with cardiologist in one week.  Cardiac rehabilitation program referral.  Close monitoring of blood glucose, lipids, and weight.  Monitor for signs and symptoms of worsening heart failure.

Prognosis:  Stable, with ongoing risk for future cardiac events and heart failure.  Prognosis is guarded, depending on adherence to medication regimen and participation in cardiac rehabilitation.  Long-term management of hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and heart failure will be crucial.
